stem: A maintenance team needs an application where technicians record inspections of equipment. Each inspection belongs to one piece of equipment and is performed by one technician, and supervisors must see each machine's inspection history. How should the Ontology be modeled before any screen is designed?

choices.text: An Inspection object type keyed on the equipment name, so that each machine has exactly one inspection object updated in place
Separate object types per equipment category, each with its own inspection properties, so screens can be tailored to each category
An Inspection object type with its own key, linked many-to-one to Equipment and to Technician, so history is a link traversal
A single Equipment object type with a list property holding inspection dates and a second list holding technician names in the same order

stem: A supervisor can open a purchase request in a Workshop module and see all its properties, but the Approve button is unavailable for them while a colleague with the same role can approve. What should the developer check first?

choices.text: Whether the supervisor's browser is outdated, since unavailable buttons are usually a rendering problem in older browsers
The Action's permissions and submission criteria against this user and object, since viewing an object does not grant permission to act on it
Whether the object type's backing dataset is stale, since stale data always disables Actions for every user who opens the object
Whether the Workshop module needs to be republished, since buttons only appear for users who opened the module after its last publish

stem: A team needs a function that computes a shipment's estimated cost from weight, distance and a tariff table, returns the same result for the same inputs, and will be maintained by engineers who already write TypeScript. Which paradigm fits?

choices.text: AIP Logic, since any function that reads Ontology data should use a language model to interpret the inputs flexibly
A Workshop variable with a formula, since all calculations belong in the application layer rather than in Functions
A scheduled pipeline transform that precomputes every possible combination of weight, distance and tariff in a dataset
A TypeScript v2 function, since the logic is deterministic, the team knows TypeScript, and no LLM capability is needed

stem: A Workshop module loads slowly. The developer finds that a hidden tab contains several object tables and charts whose variables are computed on page load even though most users never open that tab. What change addresses this most directly?

choices.text: Load the hidden tab's widgets and variables only when it is opened, and trim unneeded variable dependencies
Upgrade every user's laptop so that the browser can compute the hidden tab's variables faster on page load
Duplicate the module into two separate modules and ask users to choose which one to open each morning
Remove the hidden tab and its widgets entirely, since any content that most users do not open is unnecessary

stem: A partner-facing web portal built with the OSDK runs on the partner's servers and must call Foundry to read a curated set of objects with no end user signed in to Foundry. How should authentication be set up?

choices.text: Embed a Foundry user's personal token in the portal's front-end code, since the portal needs some credential to call the platform
Grant the application access to every object type in the Ontology so that scope errors never occur in production
Use a service-based (client credentials) application with scopes limited to the needed object types, with the secret held server-side
Ask each partner to sign in with a shared Foundry account whose password is published in the portal's help page

stem: An automation sends a shipping notice to an external carrier API when an Order becomes "Ready". Because execution is at least once, the same order occasionally produces two notices. What design makes the effect safe?

choices.text: Add a five-minute delay before the effect so that duplicate triggers have time to cancel each other out
Ask the carrier to ignore duplicate notices manually when their staff notice two messages for the same order
Disable retries on the automation so that each Ready transition can only ever be processed one time
Make the effect idempotent with a per-order idempotency key and a notified status checked first

stem: An engineer used AI FDE to generate a TypeScript function that updates order statuses. It compiles and passes a quick manual test, but the reviewer notices it loads every order in the Ontology and filters them in memory. What should happen before publishing?

choices.text: Publish it, since compiled code that passes a manual test is ready for production regardless of how it was generated
Rework it to platform idioms (server-side filtering, pagination, bounded edits), add tests, check side effects
Replace the function with a Workshop button that asks users to update each order's status by hand instead
Ask AI FDE to regenerate the function repeatedly until a version appears that the reviewer does not object to

stem: An automation creates follow-up tasks on objects that the user whose change triggered it cannot see. The user is confused, and an auditor asks how this is possible. What explains it, and what should be reviewed?

choices.text: The automation runs under its own execution identity; review that identity's permissions and who can see the tasks
The platform has a bug that leaks hidden objects to automations, and the automation should be disabled until it is fixed
The triggering user must secretly have access to the objects, and their permissions should be removed immediately to be safe
Automations always run as administrators, so nothing can or should be reviewed about what they access

stem: Three object types (Vehicle, Drone and Vessel) each have a location, a status and an operator, and a dispatch application must list all of them together and run the same Assign Operator Action on any of them. Which Ontology construct supports this cleanly?

choices.text: A dataset that unions the three backing datasets into one table, displayed in the application without any object types at all
Merge the three object types into one generic Asset type with dozens of mostly empty properties covering every kind of equipment
Three separate applications, one per object type, each with its own copy of the Assign Operator Action and list view
An interface declaring the shared properties, implemented by all three types, so the app and Action work against the interface

stem: A link between Customer and Account was configured as one-to-one, but some customers have several accounts, and the application shows only one account for them seemingly at random. What should the developer conclude and do?

choices.text: The application widget is buggy and should be replaced with a different widget that displays every linked account correctly
The cardinality does not match the data; make it one-to-many, verify with counts, and update consumers
Delete the extra accounts so that each customer has exactly one account and the one-to-one link becomes correct again
Keep the link and add a note in the application telling users that only one account is shown for each customer

stem: A claims team needs a workflow: an adjuster reviews a claim in an application, records a decision with validation, and a follow-up task is created for payments when a claim is approved. Which assembly of components fits?

choices.text: A spreadsheet export of claims that adjusters edit and email back to the payments team for manual processing
A pipeline transform that recomputes all claim decisions nightly from the adjusters' comments in a free-text field
A Workshop module for review, an Action Type for the validated decision, and an Automate step that creates the payment task on approval
A single AIP Logic function that reads the claim, decides on the adjuster's behalf and writes the payment task without any user interaction

stem: A developer must rename a property on an object type that several applications use. Before changing anything, they want to know which Workshop modules, Functions and Actions depend on it. Which capability helps most?

choices.text: Workflow Lineage, to see the applications, Functions, Actions and automations that use the object type and property
Searching through all project folders by hand and opening every module one at a time to look for the property name
Asking in the team chat whether anyone remembers using that property in their applications
Renaming the property and waiting to see which applications report errors afterwards

stem: A property "priority" appears on Ticket, Task and Incident object types and must mean the same thing with the same allowed values everywhere. Which construct ensures consistency?

choices.text: A shared property (with a value type constraining allowed values) used by all three object types
A free-text property on each type, since teams can agree informally on the wording they use
Three independent string properties defined separately on each object type, documented in a wiki page that lists the allowed values
A numeric property on each type where every team chooses its own scale of priority values

stem: Users report that edits they made to Supplier objects in an application disappeared after the backing data was refreshed. The data team says supplier codes were reformatted in the source. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Ontology edits always expire after a data refresh, so users must re-enter them every time the source updates
The edits were rejected by validation, which silently discards changes that do not match the new data format
The application failed to save the edits, and users should have clicked the save button a second time
The reformatted codes changed the primary key, so new objects appeared and the edits stayed on old keys

stem: A team proposes building a new application by copying an existing module and its Actions, then changing them, instead of reusing them. The two applications serve similar workflows for different regions. What is the better approach?

choices.text: Copy everything, since independent copies avoid coordination between the two teams that own the regional applications
Ask the original team to add the second region's screens into their module as extra tabs
Reuse shared Actions, Functions and object types, and parameterize or embed the module for regional differences
Build the second application entirely in an external tool so the two cannot interfere with each other

stem: After an object type's permissions were changed, a Workshop module shows empty tables for some users while others see data. The developer needs to find which resource in the workflow causes this. What is the most efficient approach?

choices.text: Grant the affected users Owner on every project in the workflow so that permission problems cannot occur
Trace module, object type and backing data with Workflow Lineage and access checks to find the denying layer
Tell affected users to log out and back in repeatedly until the tables start showing data
Rebuild the module from scratch on the assumption that the empty tables are caused by a corrupted layout

stem: An Action must change a Ticket's status to "Closed" and set a closed date. Another Action must close a Ticket, recalculate an SLA breach flag from several linked objects, and close all linked subtasks. Which implementation fits each?

choices.text: Function-backed for both, since any Action that edits objects should always run custom code for consistency
Declarative rules for both, since cascading edits across linked objects can always be expressed as simple property updates
Declarative edit rules for the simple close; a function-backed Action for the second, which needs computation and cascading edits
A Workshop variable for the first and an automation for the second, avoiding Actions entirely

stem: An Approve Expense Action must only be submittable when the expense is in "Submitted" status, the amount is within the approver's limit, and the approver is not the person who submitted it. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Submission criteria checking status, the user's limit and approver ≠ submitter, with clear messages
Instructions in the Workshop module's help text telling approvers which expenses they are allowed to approve
A nightly job that reverses any approval that violated the rules during the day
Hide the Approve button for every user except one administrator who checks the rules manually

stem: A user with Editor on the project can see the Action button in a module but receives a permission error when submitting it on a marked object. What explains this?

choices.text: The Action button is cached from an earlier session, and the permission error will disappear once the browser is restarted
Action execution has independent layers (Action permission, object edit permission, markings); one is missing
Editor on the project always grants permission to run every Action on every object in that project, so the platform is wrong
Actions can only be submitted by project Owners, so the user must be promoted to Owner on the project

stem: An Action succeeds for one Order but fails for another with the same form in the same module. What does the exam guide recommend investigating?

choices.text: The time of day each submission was made, since Actions are generally less reliable during busy working hours
The browser version on the user's laptop, since Action forms are known to behave differently in older browsers
The module's layout, since a UI defect is the most likely reason that identical forms behave differently
The two objects' state, links, preconditions and permissions, which explain different outcomes

stem: When a Purchase Order is approved through an Action, an external ERP must be notified. The team wants the notification tied to the Action's success. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: A nightly batch that compares approved orders with the ERP and sends any missing notifications the next day
An instruction in the Action's description reminding developers to integrate with the ERP later
Ask approvers to send an email to the ERP team after each approval so they can update the ERP manually
A webhook or side effect on the Action calling the ERP after success, retry-safe and with visible failures

stem: A developer changed an Action Type's validation and wants to test it without affecting production objects or users. What approach fits?

choices.text: Edit the Action in production and ask a few users to try it carefully on real objects during the day
Disable the Action for everyone until the change has been tested in production by the developer
Test the change on a branch with representative and invalid inputs, then review and merge
Skip testing since validation changes cannot affect users

stem: An operations manager asks the developer to remove all validation from an Action because users are complaining that it rejects their submissions. What is the right response?

choices.text: Tell users to submit the same form repeatedly until the validation accepts it
Find which rules reject submissions and why, fix wrong ones or improve messages, and keep protective validation
Remove the validation immediately, since users know their process better than the rules do
Give every complaining user administrator rights on the project so that the validation no longer applies to their submissions

stem: An Action creates a shipment and calls an external carrier API. Occasionally the carrier times out after creating the shipment on its side, the Action reports failure, and users retry, creating duplicate shipments. What should change?

choices.text: Use an idempotency key on the carrier call and record a visible operation status on the object
Add more automatic retries to the Action so that timeouts are retried immediately without involving the user
Increase the timeout to ten minutes so that the carrier always responds before the Action gives up
Tell users never to retry a failed submission under any circumstances

stem: A function that summarizes a customer's open orders works in testing but times out in production for large customers. The code traverses Customer → Orders → Line Items and loads every linked object before filtering by status in memory. What should change?

choices.text: Cache the entire Ontology in the function's memory at startup so that later traversals are faster for every customer
Increase the function's timeout so that the traversal of every linked object has enough time to complete for large customers
Filter and aggregate server-side (open orders only), page results, and bound the traversal
Move the logic into a Workshop variable so that the browser performs the traversal instead of the function

stem: A function used by three Workshop modules and one Action needs a change to its return type. The developer wants to avoid breaking the existing consumers. What is the right approach?

choices.text: Delete the function and recreate it under the same name with the new return type so that consumers pick it up
Ask every consumer owner to stop using the function permanently and write their own logic instead
Change the return type in place on the published version, since consumers always update automatically when a function changes
Publish a new function version with the new return type, migrate consumers deliberately, and keep the old version until all have moved

stem: Which requirement most clearly justifies writing a function in Python v2 rather than TypeScript v2?

choices.text: It needs a Python statistics library, and its maintainers are data scientists who work in Python
The function only sets a status property on an object, which any language can do equally well
The function must be deterministic, since only Python functions can return the same result for the same input
The function must be called from Workshop, since Workshop can only call Python functions

stem: A function-backed Action fails with an error indicating an invalid edit result. The function's code compiles and its unit test passes. What should the developer investigate?

choices.text: Whether the function should be rewritten in a different language, since edit errors are specific to the language that produced them
Whether the edits violate Ontology constraints for the real objects (types, required values, links)
Whether the user's browser has enough memory to process the returned edits
Whether the Action's button label is too long for the Workshop form that displays it

stem: A function must return the top five suppliers by on-time delivery rate in the last 90 days from millions of Delivery objects. What implementation is appropriate?

choices.text: Return all Delivery objects to Workshop and let a table widget sort them by supplier on the screen
Load all Delivery objects into the function's memory, compute rates per supplier in a loop, and sort the results in code
Use server-side filtering to the last 90 days and aggregations grouped by supplier, then order and take the top five
Ask the user to export the deliveries to a spreadsheet and compute the ranking there each week

stem: An external TypeScript application calls an Ontology function through the OSDK. After the function's signature changed, the application fails to compile. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Regenerate the OSDK package for the new function version and update the application's calls to match
Downgrade the application's TypeScript compiler to an older version that ignores type errors
Edit the generated SDK files by hand so that they match the new function signature without regenerating anything
Remove all type checking from the application so that the mismatch no longer prevents compilation

stem: A team must classify free-text maintenance notes into one of ten fault categories and then apply a deterministic routing rule by category. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: A TypeScript function that uses keyword matching to classify notes and ignores any note without an exact keyword
An AIP Logic function that both classifies the note and decides the route freely, with no structured output or rules
Manual classification by a supervisor for every note before routing
AIP Logic for the classification with a typed enum output and validation, then deterministic code that routes by category

stem: A function returns correct results for most users but an empty list for some users who should see data. The function queries objects using the calling user's permissions. What should be checked?

choices.text: Whether the function should run as an administrator so that all users see every object
Whether those users lack access to the objects (markings, restricted views, roles), since queries run as the user
Whether the users' browsers are blocking the function's results with an extension
Whether the function has an intermittent bug that only appears on certain days of the week and only for certain users

stem: A Workshop module has an object table of open tickets and a details panel that should show the ticket the user selects. How should the selection drive the panel?

choices.text: Duplicate the details panel for every ticket and hide all but one with conditional visibility
Use the table's selected-object output variable as the input to the details panel's widgets
Ask the user to type the selected ticket's id into a text box that the details panel reads
Reload the whole module each time a ticket is clicked so the panel shows the latest ticket

stem: Users report that after they submit an Action from a Workshop form, the table in the same module still shows the old value until they refresh the page. What should the developer check?

choices.text: Whether the table refreshes after the Action (an event or refresh setting) and dependent variables update
Whether users are pressing the submit button hard enough on their touchscreens
Whether the Ontology lost the edit, since a stale table always means the Action failed silently even when it reports success
Whether the module should be rebuilt in a different application to avoid caching

stem: A module must show, for a selected customer, a computed risk score from a function and let a manager trigger a review Action. How should the module connect these?

choices.text: Have the manager open a separate tool to compute the score and then return to Workshop to make edits
Copy the function's logic into a Workshop formula and build a custom form that edits the object directly without an Action
A function-backed variable for the selected customer's score, and an Action button with the customer as a parameter
Hard-code the score for each customer in the module's text widgets

stem: A Workshop module is embedded in three other modules owned by different teams. The developer wants to add a new required input variable to it. What should be considered?

choices.text: Ask the three teams to copy the module and maintain their own versions
Nothing; embedded modules always pick up new inputs automatically and supply sensible default values for every embedding
Remove the module from the other teams' applications so that the change cannot affect them
Treat the interface as a contract: add the input as optional with a default and coordinate with embedding teams

stem: A page should show an approval panel only to users when the selected request is in "Pending" status. Which Workshop feature fits?

choices.text: Two separate modules, one for pending requests and one for others
Remove the panel and ask users to check the status manually before using a separate approval module
Conditional visibility on the panel based on the selected request's status variable
A text widget asking users not to use the panel unless the request is pending

stem: A module's main table loads 50,000 objects with a dozen derived columns, and the page takes 20 seconds to open. Users usually need only today's items. What is the best first change?

choices.text: Default the table to a filtered object set (today's items) with pagination, computing derived columns only for visible rows
Keep loading all 50,000 objects with every derived column, but add a progress spinner so users know the page is working
Split the table into ten modules of 5,000 objects each
Ask users to open the module early in the morning before they need it

stem: A product team wants an AI-generated summary of each case shown in a Workshop module, generated only when the user asks. How should it be integrated?

choices.text: Generate summaries for every case in a nightly pipeline and store them, even though most of them are never viewed by anyone
Display the raw case text and label it as a summary
Ask users to copy the case text into an external chatbot and paste the summary back
A button calling an AIP Logic function for the selected case, showing the typed result with loading and error states

stem: A Workshop application is used by field staff on tablets and by managers on desktops. Field staff need large controls and few fields; managers need dense tables. What deployment approach fits?

choices.text: A single page with every control for both audiences, hidden behind tabs
Audience-specific pages or modules sharing the same Actions and Functions, each laid out for its device
One module designed for desktops only, telling field staff to zoom in on their tablets
Two completely separate applications with their own copies of every Action and Function, one for each type of device

stem: A team is building an internal React application that lets signed-in employees view and update Work Orders through the OSDK. Which setup fits?

choices.text: A service-based application with a client secret embedded in the React bundle so that every employee shares one identity
An application scoped to every object type in the Ontology so that future features never need a new scope
Direct database access from the browser to the backing datasets, bypassing the Ontology to keep the application simple
An application registered for user-based OAuth, scoped to Work Order and its Actions, with the OSDK generated for that scope

stem: An OSDK application can read Customer objects but receives an error when calling the Update Customer Action. The signed-in user can run that Action in Workshop. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Customer objects cannot be updated from any external application under any configuration
The app's scope lacks that Action; access is the intersection of the app's scope and the user's permissions
The OSDK does not support invoking Actions at all, so the application must call Workshop instead to perform any update
The user's password expired between reading the object and submitting the Action in the application

stem: An external dashboard built with the OSDK needs the total contract value per region across 2 million Contract objects. How should it be retrieved?

choices.text: Fetch all 2 million objects page by page into the dashboard and sum the contract values in the user's browser
Export the contracts to a CSV every night and have the dashboard parse the file
Use an OSDK aggregation (group by region, sum of value) so the platform returns only the totals
Call the REST API once per contract to read its value and region

stem: After a property was renamed in the Ontology, an external OSDK application started failing at runtime with field errors, although the build passed weeks ago. What should be done?

choices.text: Regenerate the OSDK, update code using the old name, and coordinate future renames through lineage
Rename the property back in the Ontology so that the external application continues to work unchanged forever
Catch and ignore the field errors in the application so that users stop seeing them
Rebuild the application with the old OSDK package, which is guaranteed to match the current Ontology

stem: Which application most clearly calls for service-based rather than user-based authentication?

choices.text: A Workshop module embedded in an internal portal for managers
A nightly integration with no user present that syncs approved orders to an ERP
A mobile application used by field staff who sign in each morning
An internal application where analysts sign in each morning and edit the objects they own through governed Actions

stem: An external application calling Foundry APIs works in testing but receives rate-limit errors in production at peak hours. What should the developer change?

choices.text: Reduce call volume (batch, aggregate, cache stable data) and add exponential backoff with jitter
Retry every failed request immediately in a tight loop until it succeeds, so that no request from any user is ever lost
Ask users to avoid using the application during peak hours
Create many separate applications with different credentials so that each stays under the limit

stem: A requirement asks for an internal approval workflow with forms, tables and charts for 200 employees. A developer proposes building a custom React application with the OSDK. What should be considered first?

choices.text: Avoiding both and using emailed spreadsheets for approvals
Building both a Workshop module and a custom React application and letting each employee decide which one to use
Always build custom applications, since they are more flexible than any native tool
Whether Workshop meets the need with less code; use the OSDK when custom UX or external users require it

stem: A public-facing portal must show customers the status of their own orders. Customers do not have Foundry accounts. How should access be designed?

choices.text: Embed a service secret in the portal's JavaScript so that the browser can call Foundry directly for each customer
Create a Foundry account for every customer and give each one Viewer on the orders project
A backend with a service client scoped to order status that authenticates customers and returns only their orders
Publish all orders on a public page and let customers search for their own order number

stem: When a Maintenance Request is created with priority "Critical", the on-call technician must be notified within minutes; other priorities should be handled in a daily digest. How should the automation be configured?

choices.text: A trigger on any property change of any Maintenance Request that sends a notification to every technician each time
A daily schedule that sends one digest containing all requests including the critical ones, delivered every morning at eight
A creation trigger conditioned on priority = Critical that notifies at once, plus a daily digest for the rest
Ask technicians to refresh the request list every few minutes and look for critical items themselves

stem: An automation calls an external ticketing API that sometimes returns transient errors. The business wants failures retried sensibly and someone informed if retries are exhausted. What should be configured?

choices.text: Bounded retries with backoff, a failure notification to the owning team on exhaustion, and recorded status
A daily manual check of the external system for missing tickets by whoever has time
Unlimited immediate retries, so that the call eventually succeeds no matter how long the external system is down
No retries, so that every transient error is visible immediately as a failure that someone must fix by hand

stem: Two automations react to the same Order update: one sets a discount, the other recalculates the total. Occasionally the total is computed before the discount is applied, producing wrong totals. What is the cause and fix?

choices.text: The Order object type is corrupted and should be recreated with new primary keys for every order
Users are editing orders too quickly; ask them to wait a minute between edits
The platform randomly reorders edits, and nothing can be done except running the recalculation again manually every evening
A race between independent automations; chain them or combine both steps into one ordered workflow

stem: A new automation will send emails to customers when their orders ship. The developer wants to verify it before it touches real customers. What is the right approach?

choices.text: Enable the automation on all orders and watch the first few hundred emails go out to real customers
Test with representative objects and a test recipient before enabling live triggers, then monitor
Skip testing, since email automations are simple and rarely fail in any way that matters
Ask a customer to confirm they received a test email in production

stem: A live automation must be changed to add a new condition. Hundreds of runs are in progress or queued. How should the change be made safely?

choices.text: Delete the automation and recreate it with the new condition, accepting the loss of queued runs
Edit the automation in place immediately; in-flight runs will simply pick up the new condition halfway through
Create a second automation with the new condition while leaving the old one running unchanged
Plan it: understand in-flight and queued runs, test the change, apply at a quiet time, and monitor

stem: Which situation is best handled by a scheduled automation rather than an event-triggered one?

choices.text: Alerting security when a sensitive object's status changes to "Compromised"
Notifying an approver the moment a high-value request is submitted
Sending a weekly summary of overdue tasks to each team lead every Monday morning
Creating a follow-up task as soon as an incident is marked resolved

stem: An automation has been failing silently for two weeks because its notifications were sent to an engineer who moved to another team. What should be fixed?

choices.text: Add every engineer in the company to the notification list so that someone always sees failures
Assign ownership to a team, route failures to its channel or rotation, and review ownership periodically
Re-route notifications to the engineer who discovered the issue, since they now know about the automation
Disable the automation since nobody noticed it was failing

stem: An automation creates an invoice in an external billing system when a contract is signed. Because Automate executes at least once, the team worries about duplicate invoices and partial failures (invoice created but status not recorded). What design handles both?

choices.text: An idempotency key per contract, status recorded after success, and a status or billing lookup before creating on retry
Run the automation only once per day to reduce the chance of duplicates
Create invoices manually instead of automating them
Trust that the automation will only ever run once per signed contract and add no further safeguards in the billing integration

stem: An application lets service agents draft a reply to a customer complaint using AI. The draft must reference the customer's open orders and must never be sent without the agent's review. How should the AI feature be built?

choices.text: A nightly pipeline that drafts replies for all complaints, which are sent automatically the next morning
A free-text box where agents paste the complaint into an external chatbot and copy the answer back into the application
An AIP Logic function that writes the reply and sends it to the customer automatically as soon as the complaint is opened
A Logic function drafting from the complaint and linked orders, shown for the agent to edit and send via an Action

stem: An AI feature summarizes a support case. The developer gave the Logic function access to all object types and every Action in the Ontology "for flexibility". What is the problem and the fix?

choices.text: There is no problem, since a model with broad access produces better summaries than one with narrow access
It breaks minimum capability; give only the case and linked objects as inputs and no write Actions
Remove the AI feature, since any AI with data access is too risky
Give the function administrator rights as well, so that it never fails on permissions

stem: An AI feature that suggests next steps for cases has become slow and costly. The trace shows a 40,000-token prompt because every linked document is injected in full. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Cache the 40,000-token prompt so that it does not need to be built again for any case
Switch to the largest available model so that it can process the long prompt faster
Trim context to relevant documents and summaries of long ones, then compare quality, latency and cost
Remove all linked documents from the prompt so that the model relies only on its general knowledge to suggest next steps

stem: AI FDE generated a function that recommends and immediately applies a discount to an order. Before publishing, what should the reviewer check specifically about side effects?

choices.text: That recommending is separated from applying via a governed Action, edits are bounded, and retries are safe
Only that the code compiles and follows the team's naming conventions
That the generated code is as short as possible
That the function produces discounts as large as possible for every order, since customers always prefer larger discounts

stem: Which requirement is a good fit for adding AI to an application rather than deterministic logic?

choices.text: Sorting a table of invoices by due date
Calculating sales tax from a jurisdiction table and an order amount
Checking that a date field is not in the future before an Action is submitted
Classifying free-text customer feedback into product themes for a review screen

stem: Users say an AI-generated "risk explanation" in an application is sometimes wrong. The developer wants evidence to decide what to fix. What should be set up?

choices.text: Switch to a different model immediately without measuring whether the new one actually produces better risk explanations
An evaluation suite of representative cases, traces of production runs, and captured user corrections
Ask the users to describe the bad explanations from memory in a monthly meeting
Hide the explanation until complaints stop

stem: An agent embedded in a module can call a "Cancel Order" Action. A user tricked it into cancelling orders belonging to other customers by pasting instructions into a comment. What is the right remediation?

choices.text: Block users from writing comments on orders
Remove all tools from every agent in the organization
Scope the tool to the order in context, apply the user's permissions and validation, and confirm cancellations
Add a sentence to the agent's system instructions telling it never to cancel orders that belong to other customers

stem: A team uses AI FDE to generate several Functions per week. Which review standard should apply before any generated Function is published?

choices.text: Full code review plus schema, platform idioms, provenance and side-effect checks, with tests and a branch run
Review only Functions longer than 200 lines, since short Functions cannot contain serious errors
Publish automatically once the generated code compiles, since generation is reliable enough for routine Functions
Ask AI FDE to review its own output and publish if it reports no problems

stem: A user can open a Workshop application but every table in it is empty, while colleagues see data. The user has Viewer on the application's project. What does the exam guide's distinction between application access and data access suggest?

choices.text: Opening the app differs from reading its data; check the user's access to the object types and backing data
Viewer on the application project automatically grants read access to all data the application displays, so the platform is malfunctioning
The application must be republished every time a new user is added so that their tables populate
The user's screen resolution is too low to display table rows, so the tables appear empty on their device only

stem: An application's Actions and Functions are developed by a small team, and production changes must be reviewed before release. Which control enforces this?

choices.text: Giving only one developer Editor rights so that nobody else can make changes at all
Branch protection requiring approval before changes merge into the production branch
A written team agreement that developers will always ask a colleague for review before merging, with no technical enforcement
A monthly audit that reverts any unreviewed change found in production

stem: An Action must create records in a restricted Audit object type that ordinary users cannot edit directly, while the Action itself is available to all users. How can this be designed safely?

choices.text: Store audit records in a free-text property on each user's profile instead
Give all users edit permission on the Audit object type so that the Action can write audit records on their behalf
Ask users to email the audit details to an administrator who creates the records manually
A function-backed Action that writes under a scoped service identity, which users may only invoke

stem: Users report that an application occasionally shows outdated object values for up to an hour after data updates. Actions and builds succeed. What operational signal should the developer check?

choices.text: The users' internet connection speed, since outdated values in applications usually come from slow or unstable networks
The number of users online, since busy periods always produce outdated values
Ontology indexing health and latency for the object type, since built data must be indexed before apps show it
The Workshop module's colour theme, which can cache values when certain themes are used

stem: Which control is appropriate for ensuring that only users in the "EMEA" region see EMEA customer rows in an application's table?

choices.text: A Workshop filter defaulting to EMEA that users can change to other regions whenever they need to see more rows
A marking named EMEA applied to the whole customer dataset
A note above the table asking non-EMEA users not to look at EMEA rows
A row-level control on the data (restricted view or object security policy) on the user's region

stem: A team operates an application with Actions, Functions and automations. They want early warning of problems before users report them. What should they monitor?

choices.text: Action failures, Function errors and latency, automation failures, indexing lag and AIP health, alerted to owners
The application's page title and logo, which change when something goes wrong
Only the number of users who opened the application each day, which shows whether the application is working as intended
Nothing, since users will report problems quickly if anything breaks

stem: To fix a user's access error in an application quickly, a colleague suggests granting the user Owner on every project the application touches. What does the exam guide recommend instead?

choices.text: Remove all permissions from the application so that every user has the same experience
Identify the exact failing permission or control and change only that, rather than over-permissioning
Create a new shared account with Owner rights that blocked users can borrow
Accept the suggestion, since unblocking the user quickly matters more than least privilege when work is waiting

stem: A scheduled automation that updates Order objects began failing after its original creator left the company. Nothing else changed. What is the likely cause and the durable fix?

choices.text: The Order object type was locked when the user left and must be unlocked by support
Give the departed user's account back its permissions so that the automation keeps working
It ran as the creator, whose access ended; move it to a team-owned, scoped service identity
The automation expired automatically because it was older than one year, and it must be recreated once every year

stem: A permit-tracking application needs a "jurisdiction" attribute on Permit, Inspection and Violation objects, always one of 40 official jurisdiction codes. Different teams own the three object types. How should the attribute be defined?

choices.text: Let each team define its own jurisdiction property in whatever format their source system uses, and reconcile the values later in each application
A separate Jurisdiction lookup application that users open to translate codes whenever they read a permit
A shared property with a value type restricting it to the 40 codes, used by all three object types
A free-text property on each object type, with a wiki page listing the 40 official codes for teams to copy from

stem: An application tracks Projects and Employees. An employee can work on many projects and a project has many employees, and the application must show each person's role and allocation percentage on each project. Which model is correct?

choices.text: A single Employee property listing every project name, separated by commas, with roles written in brackets
A many-to-many link between Project and Employee with no properties, and the role stored as a property on the Employee object
A list of employee names on each Project, with a parallel list of roles and another of allocation percentages
An Assignment object type holding role and allocation, linked many-to-one to both Project and Employee

stem: A field-service workflow must let a dispatcher assign a job, let a technician accept it on a tablet, and automatically notify the customer once accepted. Which assembly fits the guide's lifecycle?

choices.text: A single AIP agent that assigns, accepts and notifies on its own, without any user interaction or confirmation
A dispatcher module with an Assign Action, a technician module with an Accept Action, and an automation notifying the customer on acceptance
A spreadsheet shared by dispatchers and technicians, with customers emailed from personal inboxes when someone remembers
One Workshop page where the dispatcher edits job properties directly in a table, and the customer is notified manually by phone after the technician calls in

stem: After a link type between Supplier and Contract was deleted during a cleanup, two applications and a scheduled automation started failing. The developer did not know they depended on it. What practice would have prevented this?

choices.text: Checking Workflow Lineage for consumers of the link type before the change, then migrating them or keeping the link
Never deleting anything from the Ontology, so that unused resources accumulate indefinitely
Asking users to report failures quickly so that the link can be recreated after the fact
Deleting link types only on Fridays, so that any failures happen over the weekend when fewer users are affected

stem: Which statement about modelling before designing screens reflects the guide's recommended approach?

choices.text: Design the screens first and create whatever object types the screens happen to need, one per screen
Skip the Ontology and bind screens directly to datasets, since modelling slows development down
Store all data in one object type with generic columns so that any screen can display anything it needs
Model meaningful objects and links with stable identity first, then design the interface on top of that model

stem: A link between Order and Customer is backed by a customer id column, but many orders show no linked customer in the application although the customer exists. What should the developer check?

choices.text: Whether customers need to be re-created every time a new order is placed
Whether link types only display the first hundred links ever created in the Ontology
Whether the foreign key values match the customer primary keys exactly (format, case, padding) and whether the user can see those customers
Whether the application's layout hides linked objects when the screen is narrower than a certain width

stem: A team wants a workflow where AI suggests a resolution category for each incident and an analyst confirms it. They debate storing the AI suggestion and the confirmed category in the same property. What is the better design?

choices.text: Separate properties for the AI suggestion and the confirmed category, with the confirmation written by an Action
One property overwritten by the AI and then by the analyst, since only the final value matters to anyone
Store neither and let analysts type the category into a comment field
Store only the AI suggestion and treat it as final, since analysts usually agree with it

stem: A user reports they cannot see a new module's data, while the developer can. The module reads two object types, one backed by a restricted view. What is the most efficient way to locate the cause?

choices.text: Grant the user Owner on every project in the workflow, then remove permissions one at a time until the module breaks again
Follow the module's dependencies with Workflow Lineage and check the user's access at each layer, especially the restricted view's policy
Recreate the module under the user's account so that it uses their permissions from the start
Ask the user to clear their browser cache and try again every few hours

stem: A Create Purchase Request Action has a form with ten fields, but users frequently submit requests with a missing cost centre or an amount in the wrong currency. How should the form and Action be improved?

choices.text: Add a paragraph of instructions at the top of the form and trust users to read it before submitting
Make the cost centre a required parameter chosen from valid values, constrain currency, and validate again at submission
Leave the form as it is and correct bad requests manually after they have been submitted and noticed by the finance team
Remove the cost centre field from the form entirely, since users find it confusing and keep getting it wrong

stem: An Action updates a Shipment's status. A developer proposes rewriting it as a function-backed Action "for future flexibility", although the current logic is a single property update with one validation rule. What is the better choice?

choices.text: Keep it declarative, since it is a direct governed edit; convert only when real computation is needed
Rewrite it as function-backed now, since function-backed Actions are always preferable regardless of complexity
Replace the Action with a Workshop variable that edits the property directly
Remove validation so that the declarative Action is even simpler

stem: A Delete Customer Action should be available only to the data stewardship group, while everyone can view customers. How should this be configured?

choices.text: Hide the Delete button in the Workshop module for everyone except stewards, without changing the Action itself
Give the stewardship group Owner on every project that contains customer data
Restrict the Action's permissions to the stewardship group, so only its members can run it through any application or API
Add a confirmation dialog asking users whether they are a steward before deleting

stem: Users report that an Action "does nothing": they submit it, see no error, but the object does not change. Execution logs show the Action succeeded. What should the developer check?

choices.text: Whether the Ontology ignores edits from users who joined recently
Whether the Action needs to be deleted and recreated to start working
Whether users are clicking the button twice, since a second click always cancels the first submission
Whether the edit rules target the intended object and property, and the module refreshes

stem: Which requirement is best implemented as an Action's submission criteria rather than as form-level input validation alone?

choices.text: A date picker should default to today
A text field must not exceed 500 characters
An approver cannot approve their own request, checked against the object and user at execution
A dropdown in the form should list all departments in alphabetical order so that users find theirs quickly

stem: An Action that edits Invoice objects fails for a group of users with a permission error, although they have Editor on the project. The invoices carry a "Finance" marking. What is the right fix?

choices.text: Give the users administrator rights so that markings no longer apply to them
Copy the invoices into an unmarked project so that the Action can edit the copies there instead of the originals
Remove the Finance marking from all invoices so that every Editor can run the Action
Decide whether they should handle finance data; if so, grant the marking via its owner

stem: An Action changes a loan application's status and must leave an audit trail showing who changed it, when, and why. What should the Action include?

choices.text: An email to the compliance team after each change, written by the user
A required reason parameter stored with the change, plus execution history for who and when
Nothing extra, since the Ontology does not need to record who changed an object or for what reason the change was made
A shared spreadsheet where users log their changes manually

stem: Approving a claim must update the claim, create a payment object, adjust the policy's remaining coverage, and all three changes must succeed or fail together. How should this be implemented?

choices.text: One function-backed Action validating preconditions and returning all three edits together
A declarative Action for the claim and an automation that later creates the payment and adjusts coverage
A Workshop button that edits the three objects directly through variables
Three separate declarative Actions that users run one after another in the correct order

stem: A function must return each warehouse's count of overdue shipments for a dashboard of 300 warehouses, computed from millions of Shipment objects. Which implementation is appropriate?

choices.text: Return every Shipment object to the dashboard and let a chart widget count overdue items per warehouse in the browser
Filter shipments to overdue status server-side and aggregate counts grouped by warehouse, returning one row per warehouse
Ask each warehouse manager to count their overdue shipments manually and type the number into a form every morning
Iterate over all Shipment objects in the function, checking each one's due date and counting overdue shipments per warehouse in a dictionary

stem: A team wants confidence that a pricing function behaves correctly before publishing a new version. What testing approach fits?

choices.text: Unit tests on representative and edge inputs plus a branch run against real objects before publishing
Test only the happy path with one typical example, since edge cases such as missing tariffs rarely occur in practice
Ask the AI assistant whether the function is correct and publish if it agrees
Publish the new version and watch production for complaints during the first week

stem: A function needs to call an external currency API and parse its response, and it is maintained by engineers fluent in TypeScript. Another candidate implementation uses AIP Logic to "interpret" the API response. Which is better?

choices.text: A Workshop formula that calls the API directly from the browser on each page load
AIP Logic, since language models are good at reading API responses and adapting to format changes automatically
A TypeScript v2 function with explicit parsing and error handling for the structured response
Manual entry of exchange rates by finance staff each morning

stem: A function computes a credit limit used by an Action. Auditors want to know, for any approved limit, which version of the logic produced it. What should be in place?

choices.text: A comment in the code noting the date of each change
A spreadsheet where developers note which version they think was live each month
Nothing, since auditors can always read the current function code to infer how past values were computed
Published function versions, with the Action recording the version used alongside the result

stem: A function that traverses Customer → Orders → Items → Supplier for a single customer works in development but times out for some customers in production. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The development environment has faster networking, which explains why the function only times out in production
The customers with timeouts have corrupted data that must be deleted
An unbounded multi-hop traversal loading huge object counts for large customers; bound it
The production function is out of date and needs to be republished with the same code to start working

stem: A developer is explaining to a new team member how function-backed Actions apply their changes and how they are governed. Which statement about function-backed Actions is correct?

choices.text: Function-backed Actions cannot edit more than one object
The function returns edits that the Action applies after validation, so the result is governed by the Action's permissions and criteria
A function-backed Action applies edits as the function executes, one by one, so partial results are visible if it fails midway
A function-backed Action bypasses the Action's submission criteria because the function is trusted

stem: A function called from Workshop returns correct results when the developer runs it but an error for analysts: "object type not found". What is the likely cause?

choices.text: The analysts are using a different browser that does not support the function's return type when it is displayed in Workshop
The analysts' module is in a different time zone
The function is too slow for analysts, so the platform cancels it with a misleading message
The function queries an object type analysts cannot see; under user-scoped execution it looks missing

stem: A team must implement routing logic that assigns incoming cases to queues using fifteen explicit business rules, plus a free-text field that occasionally needs interpretation when no rule applies. Who will maintain it: business analysts who change rules monthly. What design fits?

choices.text: Rules in deterministic code driven by a governed rules dataset analysts can update, with an AI step only for unmatched cases
A TypeScript function with all fifteen rules hard-coded, released by engineers every time analysts want a change
Manual routing by a supervisor reading every case
An AIP Logic function that applies all fifteen rules from a long prompt and interprets the free text in the same call

stem: In a Workshop module, a chart depends on a filter variable, and a table depends on the chart's selection. Users report the table sometimes shows data for the previous filter after they change it. What is likely happening?

stem: A module serves several user steps: search for a case, review details, and record a decision. Users get lost in one long scrolling page. What design improves usability?

Remove the decision step and record decisions by email instead
Create a separate module for each step and ask users to copy the case id between modules

stem: A module must show a list of a manager's direct reports and, for each, a computed "workload score" from a function. The list can have up to 50 people. How should it be built?

choices.text: An object table of the manager's reports with a function-backed workload column
Call the workload function separately from 50 text widgets, each configured by hand for one employee
Ask managers to compute workload in a spreadsheet and upload it to the module
Hard-code each employee's workload into the module and update it monthly

Embedded modules randomly lose connections over time, and parent modules must be rebuilt periodically

stem: A module recomputes an expensive function-backed variable every time any filter changes, even filters unrelated to it. Users find the module sluggish. What is the best refactor?

Add a loading spinner over the whole module while the variable recomputes
Remove all filters from the module so that the expensive variable is computed only once when the page loads

stem: Which is the most appropriate way for a Workshop module to let users change an object's status?

choices.text: An Action button or inline Action that runs the configured Action Type with validation and permissions
A link to the backing dataset where users edit the value directly
An editable table cell bound directly to the status property, with no Action, validation or audit trail behind it
A text box where users type the new status and a developer applies it later

stem: A module should display a warning banner when the selected order's delivery date is in the past and its status is not "Delivered". How should this be built?

choices.text: A separate module showing all overdue orders that users must open alongside the main one
A derived boolean variable controlling the banner's conditional visibility
Ask users to compare the dates themselves and remember to check the status
A daily email listing overdue orders to all users

Edit the live module directly during business hours and fix whatever problems users report as the redesign progresses

stem: An internal OSDK application works for most employees, but one team receives authentication errors after signing in. Their accounts are in a different organization than the application's resources. What should be checked?

stem: Which task is best done by invoking an Action through the OSDK rather than writing data another way?

choices.text: Reading a list of open tickets with their priorities to display in an external dashboard for the support team

Changing a ticket's status from an external application with validation and audit

choices.text: No authentication for the screen, since it is internal and only employees can reach it

stem: A product team wants to embed a Foundry-backed view inside their existing customer-support web application rather than sending agents to a separate Foundry tab. What approach fits?

Retry every few seconds indefinitely until the partner responds, regardless of how long the outage lasts

Stop the whole automation and all other workflows until the partner confirms recovery

stem: An automation in a shared project is owned by an individual, and its failures go to their personal inbox. The team wants operations to be resilient to people changing roles. What should be configured?

Duplicate the automation under each team member's name so that someone always owns a copy
Team ownership with notifications to a team channel or rotation, and the project scope reviewed

stem: An automation runs when an Invoice is approved and posts it to an accounting system. Users sometimes approve and then immediately reject an invoice. What must the design handle?

stem: A team must change an automation's condition and effect for a critical billing workflow. They need confidence before it affects real customers. What sequence is appropriate?

stem: An application needs AI to extract the due date, amount and vendor from uploaded invoices so a clerk can confirm them before an Action creates the payable. How should the AIP Logic function's output be defined?

stem: An agent embedded in a sales application should answer questions about the selected account's opportunities. Which configuration follows the minimum-capability principle?

stem: Users say an AI summary feature in a Workshop module sometimes states facts not present in the case. What should the developer do first?

stem: An AI FDE-generated Function passes its tests, but a reviewer notices it writes to an object type that does not exist in the current Ontology schema under that name. What should happen?

stem: Which design best uses an agent in an application rather than a single AIP Logic function?

choices.text: A conversational assistant answering varied follow-ups about a case using scoped lookup tools

Extracting the same three fixed fields from each uploaded document in exactly the same way every time it runs

stem: A cost report shows an AI feature calls the model on every page load for every user, even when the underlying case has not changed. What should the developer change?

stem: Before releasing an AI-backed Action that proposes refund amounts for agents to confirm, the team wants evidence of quality. What should the evaluation include?

Only the cases where the AI is known to perform well

stem: AI FDE produced a Function that updates customer tiers and also calls an external marketing API. The team must decide whether it is safe to publish. Which review points are most important for side-effect safety?

Whether the Function compiles on the reviewer's laptop

stem: An application shows Employee objects to all staff, but the salary property must be visible only to HR, while other properties remain visible to everyone. Which control fits?

choices.text: Remove the salary property from the Ontology entirely so that nobody, including HR, can see it in any application

stem: A user cannot open an application at all and receives a resource permission error, while their teammates can. The data the application shows is not sensitive. What should be checked first?

Whether the user's data permissions on the underlying datasets include every marking that exists in the organization

stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes user-scoped from project-scoped execution for an Action or Function?

stem: An application's automation started failing at 03:00 and users noticed at 09:00. The team wants to detect this kind of failure within minutes in future. What should be set up?

choices.text: Alerts on failed and missing runs, routed to the owning team's rotation, with a runbook
Ask users to report problems as soon as they arrive at work in the morning
A weekly review meeting where the whole team looks through the automation's run history together on a shared screen
Restart the automation every night at 02:55 to prevent failures at 03:00

stem: An application team wants all members to be able to merge changes to production Actions instantly to move faster. A security reviewer objects. What is a balanced approach?

choices.text: Branch protection with required review, kept fast with small changes and quick branch builds
Allow merges only once a quarter in a large release
Let everyone merge directly to production, since speed is more important than review for internal applications
Freeze all changes to production Actions permanently so that nothing can go wrong

stem: A module is shared with a partner organization's users, who should see only partner-related objects. Internal users see everything. How should access be designed?

choices.text: Copy the partner objects into a separate dataset each night and email it to the partner
Give the partner's users the module and data-level controls limiting them to partner objects
Share the module with the partner organization and rely on the module's filters to hide internal objects from them

stem: A function-backed Action runs project-scoped under a service identity. After a security review, the identity's permissions were reduced, and now the Action fails for everyone. What should the developer do?

Restore the identity's original broad permissions immediately so that the Action works again
Identify exactly what the Action reads and writes, grant only that to the identity, and test
Delete the Action and ask users to edit objects directly

stem: Users report that an AI-assisted application has become slow and occasionally returns errors since yesterday. The application uses Ontology queries, a Function and an AIP Logic call. How should the developer locate the cause efficiently?

Switch the AIP Logic call to a larger model, since AI is usually the slowest part
Rewrite all three components in parallel, assuming they are all responsible for the slowdown
Use per-component monitoring and traces to find which step's latency or errors changed

Address corrections are not supported by the Ontology, so the source team should stop correcting addresses

stem: An insurance application models Policies, and each policy can have many Coverages of different types with different properties (auto coverage has vehicle fields, home coverage has property fields). How should coverages be modelled?

choices.text: One Coverage object type with every possible field for every coverage kind, most of them empty for any given coverage
One object type per policy, with coverage fields added as new properties each time a policy adds a coverage
Coverage details stored as one long JSON text property on the Policy object, parsed by each application

stem: A team designs a returns workflow. One proposal puts all logic (eligibility, refund calculation, warehouse notification, customer email) into a single Workshop button script. Another separates them into components. Which design is better and why?

Skip automation and ask the warehouse to check a list of returns every afternoon

stem: An auditor asks which applications and automations can change Contract objects, and which Actions they use. What is the most efficient way to answer?

Use Workflow Lineage on Contract to list its Actions and the modules and automations using them

Search the codebase for the word "contract" and assume every match changes Contract objects

stem: Which link cardinality correctly models "each Ticket is assigned to at most one Agent at a time, and an Agent handles many Tickets"?

stem: A hospital wants an application where nurses record vital signs, and a doctor is alerted when readings cross thresholds. Nurses work on tablets; doctors receive alerts on their phones. Which assembly fits?

An AI agent that reads all vitals continuously and decides on its own whether to call a doctor
A tablet Record Vitals Action, a threshold automation, and a notification to the doctor
A spreadsheet that nurses update and doctors check every hour on their phones

stem: Two teams created separate "Customer" object types for their applications. Reports now disagree on customer counts, and links from Orders point to one type or the other. What should be done?

choices.text: Keep both object types and ask report authors to sum them, accepting some double counting
Delete one team's object type immediately, regardless of the applications that depend on it
Rename one type to "Customer2" so that the two are easier to tell apart
Consolidate on one Customer type with a stable key and migrate links, edits and apps

stem: A property used by eight applications must change its meaning (from "estimated cost" to "approved cost"). Some applications need the old meaning for six more months. What is the safest approach?

Submission criteria on the Action checking the target agent's team and leave status at execution, with a clear message
Show a warning text in the form reminding team leads to check the new agent's team and leave status before submitting
Remove the reassign capability and let tickets stay with their original agent indefinitely

stem: An Action's execution history shows frequent failures with a validation message that the "end date must be after start date", but users insist they entered valid dates. What should the developer investigate?

Whether the validation should be deleted, since users keep hitting it

stem: A Mark Delivered Action needs to set the status, record the delivery time, and increment the customer's delivered-orders count on a linked Customer object. Which implementation fits?

choices.text: A function-backed Action that edits the order and recomputes the linked customer's count, applied together
Three separate declarative Actions that users must run one after another for each delivered order

stem: Which statement about the security layers involved when a user runs an Action is correct?

choices.text: Markings do not apply to objects edited through Actions

Ask technicians to retype every work order into the CMMS manually at the end of each day

stem: A developer wants to verify that a revised Approve Action rejects invalid cases and accepts valid ones before release, including permission differences. Which test plan fits?

choices.text: Release the change to production and watch how many approvals fail or succeed during the first week of use
Ask one team lead to try the Action on a real object and report back
Test once as the developer, who has every permission, with one valid object
Branch tests with valid, invalid and edge cases, as users with and without permission

stem: An Action currently uses declarative rules. A new requirement adds a calculation of a late fee based on days overdue and the customer's tier. What is the right change?

Remove the late fee requirement because declarative Actions cannot handle it

Add a nightly job that calculates late fees for every record and overwrites whatever was submitted

stem: A user can submit an Action that edits Project objects, but for one project the submission fails with a permission error while others succeed. The Action and the user's groups are unchanged. What is the most likely explanation and next step?

The platform randomly rejects some submissions, so the user should retry until it works

stem: A function must update the status of all open tasks linked to a project when the project is cancelled. Projects can have up to 5,000 tasks. How should the edits be implemented safely?

stem: Which function requirement is the clearest case for AIP Logic rather than TypeScript or Python code?
