That automations are trusted by default and need no documentation
The execution identity, its minimal permissions, what it writes where, who sees the output, and its owner

stem: An application team wants a single view of their application's operational health: Action failures, Function latency, automation runs, Ontology indexing status and AI usage. What should they build and how should it be used?

choices.text: A view showing only daily active users, reviewed once a quarter by the product owner
A monitoring view of those signals with thresholds routed to the owning team, runbooks and reviews
A spreadsheet that developers update manually when they notice problems
Nothing extra, since each component already shows its own errors to users in the application whenever something fails

stem: A logistics app needs to show each Truck's current driver and the full history of which drivers drove it and when. Drivers change trucks often. How should this be modelled for both the current view and the history?

choices.text: A separate Truck object for each driver who has ever driven it, so each copy holds exactly one driver
A single "driver" property on Truck that is overwritten at each change, with history reconstructed from old screenshots if anyone needs it
A DriverAssignment object type with start and end times linked to Truck and Driver, plus a derived current-driver link on Truck
A list property on Truck holding every driver's name in the order they drove it, with no times recorded anywhere

stem: Which choice of primary key for an Employee object type is most stable?

choices.text: The row number of the employee in the backing dataset, since it is always unique within a build
The employee's email address, since it is unique and easy to read for anyone looking at the data
The employee's full name combined with their department, since that combination is usually unique
The employee number assigned once by the HR system of record and never reused

stem: A procurement workflow needs: requesters submit purchase requests, a policy check runs automatically, approvers decide, and approved requests create purchase orders in an external ERP. Which assembly fits?

choices.text: A request Action, an automation running a policy Function, an approval module and Action, then an automation calling the ERP
A single AIP Logic function that reads the request, decides approval and writes to the ERP without human involvement
Requesters email approvers, who forward approved emails to the purchasing team for manual ERP entry
A spreadsheet of requests reviewed weekly by finance, with approved rows uploaded to the ERP manually

stem: After a developer changed a link type's cardinality from one-to-many to many-to-many, a Workshop module started showing errors and an automation stopped running. What should have been done first?

choices.text: Make the change on a Friday evening so that fewer users notice the errors
Review the link's consumers in Workflow Lineage and migrate them on a branch first
Delete the module and the automation before making any Ontology change, then rebuild them later
Nothing different; cardinality changes never affect existing consumers, so the errors must be unrelated

stem: A team wants to add 40 rarely used properties to a core Customer object type because one new application needs them. Other applications use Customer heavily. What is a sensible approach?

choices.text: Model the new data as a linked object type (for example CustomerProfileDetail) used by the new application, keeping Customer focused
Add all 40 properties to Customer immediately, since more properties on a core type never cause problems for other applications
Store the 40 values as one JSON text property on Customer so the type's schema does not change
Create a second Customer object type for the new application with all existing and new properties copied over

stem: A link from Invoice to Customer uses the customer code on the invoice. For one source system, codes have a prefix ("ACME-C123") while the Customer key is "C123". Those invoices show no customer. What is the correct fix?

choices.text: Change every Customer key to include the prefix, breaking the other systems' links
Ask users to look up customers manually for invoices from that source system
Add the prefixed codes as additional primary keys on the Customer object type so that both forms of the code match
Normalize the foreign key to the Customer key format and check every invoice resolves

stem: Which component should own each step of "a user submits a leave request, and if approved, the HR system is updated"?

choices.text: A Workshop variable submits the request, and a Function updates the HR system directly from the browser
Actions for submission and approval, and an automation updating the HR system afterwards
A pipeline transform submits requests nightly and updates the HR system from a dataset
An AIP agent submits, approves and updates on its own without any user confirmation

stem: A team must change the primary key of a heavily used object type because the old key was unstable. Many applications, Functions and user edits depend on it. What plan fits?

choices.text: Create a new object type with the new key and leave the old one running forever alongside it
Change the key in place during business hours and ask users to re-enter any of their edits that happen to disappear
Map old to new keys, migrate edits and links, update consumers on a branch, then validate
Postpone the change indefinitely, since key changes are always too risky to attempt

stem: A Schedule Maintenance Action takes a date parameter. Users sometimes pick dates in the past or on public holidays, causing rework. How should the Action handle this?

choices.text: Accept any date and let the maintenance team reschedule invalid bookings by phone after they notice them
Limit the date to future dates and validate against a holiday reference at submission
Add a note under the date field asking users not to choose holidays or past dates
Remove the date parameter and schedule all maintenance for the first day of the next month

stem: An Action works when tested by the developer on a branch, but after merge it fails for all users with a validation error referencing a property that exists only on the branch. What went wrong?

choices.text: Branch testing is unreliable, so Actions should be tested directly in production instead
The platform deleted the property during the merge as part of its normal cleanup of branch resources
The Action merged before the Ontology change adding the property it uses
Users lack a special permission that only the developer has for properties created on branches

stem: Which requirement can be met with a declarative Action rather than a function-backed one?

choices.text: Resolve an Incident and close all of its linked child tasks, cascading through several levels of links
Close an Incident and recompute the SLA breach flag from the incident's timeline of linked events
Resolve an Incident and calculate a penalty amount based on contract terms stored on a linked Contract
Set an Incident's status to Resolved and record the resolver and time

stem: An Action lets agents issue goodwill credits. Agents may issue up to 50; team leads up to 500; above that requires finance. How should this be implemented?

choices.text: Criteria comparing the amount with the user's role limit, plus an approval path above 500
Let anyone issue any amount and have finance audit the credits once a quarter
Three separate Actions with no limits, and trust that people use the one matching their role
One Action available to everyone, with a note in the form explaining the credit limits that apply to each role

stem: A webhook configured on an Action posts to an external system. Users report that the Action succeeds but the external system sometimes has no record. Execution evidence shows occasional webhook errors that users never see. What should change?

choices.text: Nothing, since the Action succeeded and the external system is not the developer's responsibility
Make the Action fail whenever the webhook fails, even if the Ontology change is already valid
Remove the webhook and ask users to update the external system manually after every Action
Surface webhook failures with status and alerts, retry idempotently, and allow resending

stem: An auditor asks the team to prove that a specific Approve Payment Action was executed by an authorized user with valid inputs last March. What evidence should the developer provide?

choices.text: A screenshot of the current Action configuration taken today
The source code of the Workshop module that displays the Approve button
Execution history (user, time, inputs, outcome) plus the permissions and criteria then
A written statement from the team confirming that the Action has always worked correctly since the day it was released

stem: An Action creates a Booking and must also reserve inventory on a linked Product. Occasionally two users book the last unit at the same time, and both succeed, overselling. What design addresses this?

choices.text: A function-backed Action checking availability and reserving atomically, failing on conflict
Restrict booking to one user per day so that conflicts cannot happen
Ask users to check inventory in a separate screen before booking and trust them to notice the last unit
Allow overselling and reconcile with customers by email at the end of the week

stem: After a reorganization, an entire team cannot run the Close Case Action they used yesterday. They can still view cases. No one changed the Action. What is the most likely cause and the correct fix?

choices.text: The Action has a daily usage quota that the team exhausted yesterday, so they must wait until tomorrow
Their group membership changed and no longer matches the Action's permitted groups
The cases became read-only for everyone overnight, so nobody in the company can close them
Grant the team administrator rights on the project so that they can run any Action

stem: A function must find all Equipment objects at a site that have no inspection in the last 90 days. Sites have up to 3,000 pieces of equipment, each with many inspections. Which approach is efficient?

choices.text: Query equipment at the site and use a server-side filter or aggregation on linked inspections in the last 90 days to find those with none
Load every piece of equipment and every inspection into memory, then compare dates for each piece in nested loops inside the function
Ask inspectors to keep a spreadsheet of equipment they have not inspected recently and upload it each week
Return all equipment to Workshop and let users scroll through each item's inspection history manually

stem: A function-backed Action fails for some objects with an error that a linked object could not be found. The function traverses Order → Customer and reads the customer's tier. What should be checked?

choices.text: Whether the Action's form is too wide for the screen, which can hide linked objects from the function at execution
Whether the function should catch all errors and continue silently with a default tier
Whether some orders lack a resolvable or visible customer, and handle that case explicitly
Whether all customers should be deleted and recreated so that the links are rebuilt from scratch

stem: A function must generate a polite rejection email for job applicants based on structured reasons, and the HR team wants the tone adjustable without code changes. Which paradigm and setup fit?

choices.text: A Python function that sends the same fixed sentence to every applicant regardless of the reason
A TypeScript function with hard-coded email templates, updated by developers whenever HR asks for different wording
Have HR write each rejection email manually without any assistance
AIP Logic with the reasons as typed input, HR-maintained tone guidance, and review before sending

stem: Which practice best supports reliable use of a function by an external application through the OSDK?

choices.text: Changing the function's return type whenever convenient, since external apps can adapt automatically at runtime
Publishing versions, documenting the return type, and regenerating the OSDK when the function changes
Returning untyped text so that external apps can parse whatever they need
Hiding the function from the OSDK and asking external developers to call internal endpoints directly

stem: A function that sums revenue per region returns correct results for small regions but times out for the largest region. Profiling shows it loads all Sale objects for the region and sums in code. What is the fix?

choices.text: Split the largest region into smaller fake regions so each one fits within the time limit
Ask users from the largest region to avoid using the function at busy times
Raise the function's timeout limit so that the largest region's sum has enough time to finish loading
Use a server-side aggregation (sum grouped by region) instead of loading individual Sale objects

stem: A team wants to prevent regressions in a function used by a high-traffic Action. Changes are made weekly. What should be in place?

choices.text: No tests, but a quick rollback if users complain after the weekly change
Unit tests run on every change, a branch run on real objects, and versioned publishing
Tests written once at the start of the project and never updated
Manual spot checks by the developer who made the change, done on a couple of objects before publishing

stem: An Action uses a function to compute insurance premiums. Regulators require that any premium can be reproduced later. What should the Action record?

choices.text: The premium, the function version and the input values used
A link to the function's source code repository and nothing else
The name of the developer who last edited the function
Only the final premium amount, since the function can always recompute it later from current data

stem: A team is choosing how to implement a function that classifies documents by type. A rule-based TypeScript version reaches 85% accuracy; an AIP Logic version reaches 96% on the evaluation set but costs more per call. Volume is 2,000 documents a day, and misclassification causes manual rework. What should guide the decision?

choices.text: Always choose the AIP Logic version, since higher accuracy always wins regardless of cost
Always choose the TypeScript version, since deterministic code is better than AI in every case regardless of accuracy
Weigh rework from the accuracy gap against AI cost at this volume, considering rules first and AI for the rest
Choose whichever version the most senior developer prefers

stem: A module needs a map of sites, a list of the selected site's assets, and a form to create a work order for the selected asset. How should the widgets be connected?

choices.text: Three independent widgets where users must re-select the site and the asset separately in each one
Three separate modules, one per widget, with users copying identifiers between them
One giant table containing every site and asset together, with a free-text field for typing the asset id into the form
Chain map selection → site variable → filtered asset list → asset variable → Action parameter

stem: A dashboard module recomputes a heavy aggregation every time a user switches tabs, even though the data has not changed. Users find tab switching slow. What should be changed?

choices.text: Ask users to stay on one tab per session
Add a spinner on each tab so users understand the delay
Compute the aggregation outside the tabs' lifecycle so tab switches reuse it
Remove the tabs and put all content on one long page so that nothing needs to recompute on navigation

stem: Which is the right way to show a list of a customer's open tickets in a Workshop module?

choices.text: A text widget where a developer pastes ticket numbers by hand each morning
An object table bound to the selected customer's linked open-ticket object set
A spreadsheet download link that users open in another program
An image of the ticket system's screen refreshed weekly

stem: A team builds the same "customer header" (name, tier, contact, risk badge) in five different modules, each slightly different. Maintenance is painful. What should they do?

choices.text: One reusable header module with a customer input, embedded in all five modules
Merge all five modules into one enormous module with every page
Remove the header from all modules to avoid maintenance
Keep all five versions of the header and update each one by hand in its own module whenever the design changes

stem: A module triggers an Action and then immediately reads a property the Action updates. Sometimes the read returns the old value. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Refresh the dependent widgets from the Action's completion event
Read the property twice and use the second value
Ask users to click a refresh button whenever values look wrong
Add a fixed delay of several seconds after the Action before reading the property, and hope it is enough

stem: A filter dropdown in a module shows only 50 values, but there are 300 regions. Users cannot find their region. What should the developer check?

choices.text: Whether users should type the region into a free-text field instead
The dropdown's data source and limits; use a searchable filter that supports all values
Whether regions beyond the first 50 were deleted from the Ontology
Whether the users' screens are too small to display a dropdown list longer than fifty entries without scrolling

stem: A module needs a "risk score" per row in a table of 500 contracts. The score can come from a function computing it on the fly or from a property materialized nightly. Users sort by it and the score changes daily. Which is better?

choices.text: Ask users to compute risk scores in a spreadsheet and enter them manually
Hide the risk score since it cannot be both fast and current
A materialized property for display and sorting, with live detail for the selected contract
A function-backed column computed live for all 500 rows every time the table loads or is sorted

stem: A team wants to add a major new page to a module used daily by 300 people, but the page's queries are heavy and not yet tuned. How should they release it?

choices.text: Add the page to the live module immediately and tune its performance later, based on whatever complaints users send
Build the page as a separate module and stop maintaining the original
Never add new pages to busy modules
Develop and tune on a branch, pilot with a small group, then release with monitoring

stem: A team is registering a new external application that will read Products and invoke a Create Quote Action for signed-in sales staff. Which registration settings matter most for security?

choices.text: User-based OAuth, scopes limited to Products and Create Quote, and exact redirect URLs per environment
Request every scope available in the Ontology so that future features never require changes to the application's registration
No registration at all; call the Ontology anonymously from the browser to keep the setup simple
A shared service secret embedded in the app so that sales staff do not have to sign in each time they use it

stem: An external app invokes an Approve Order Action through the OSDK. Some calls fail with a validation error that the Workshop version of the same Action shows to users as a friendly message. External users see a generic "error" instead. What should the developer do?

choices.text: Remove the Action's validation so that external calls never fail with validation errors
Call the Action twice to increase the chance of success
Show users the Action's specific validation message instead of a generic error
Retry the Action automatically until the validation passes

stem: Which statement about user-based and service-based authentication for OSDK applications is correct?

choices.text: User-based authentication requires embedding a client secret in the browser to work properly
Service-based and user-based authentication give identical access results for every user
Service-based authentication should always be preferred because it never requires users to sign in to anything
User-based auth applies each user's permissions; service-based suits headless processes

stem: An external app was working until a new OSDK package version was installed. Now some object fields come back undefined. The developer did not change the code. What is likely and what should be done?

choices.text: The Ontology lost data during the package upgrade, so the data team must restore it from backups
The new package reflects a changed Ontology; review the types, update the code, and pin versions
The users' browsers need clearing; undefined fields are always a caching problem
The OSDK randomly drops fields on new installs, so the app should be reinstalled until the fields return

stem: An external dashboard needs to show, every few seconds, the count of open alerts per site for 500 sites. What is the most efficient approach?

choices.text: Fetch every alert object every few seconds and count the open alerts for each site in the user's browser
Call the API once per site every few seconds, making 500 requests each time
A grouped aggregation (count of open alerts by site) on a sensible refresh interval, with caching
Export alerts to a file every minute and have the dashboard parse it

stem: An internal team asks whether to build a new approval tool in Workshop or as a custom web app with the OSDK. Users are internal, the UI is forms and tables, and the team has little front-end experience. What should guide the choice?

choices.text: Build both and let users vote on which one they prefer after a month
Always build a custom web app, since custom apps are more professional than native tools
Use neither and keep approvals in email
Prefer Workshop when it meets an internal forms-and-tables need; use the OSDK for custom needs

stem: An external app's calls fail intermittently with rate-limit errors during a nightly import that loops over 50,000 objects and calls an Action for each. What change best fits?

choices.text: Batch where possible, pace calls with backoff, and make Action calls idempotent
Run the import during business hours when more capacity is available
Remove all delays from the import loop so that it finishes faster before rate limits apply
Split the import across many separately registered applications to multiply the rate limit

stem: A partner integration currently uses a long-lived service secret that was emailed to the partner two years ago and never rotated. The security team asks for remediation. What is the right plan?

choices.text: Disable the integration permanently since secrets are inherently insecure
Issue a new scoped credential securely, migrate the partner, revoke the old secret, and rotate it
Leave the secret in place since nothing bad has happened in two years
Email the same long-lived secret again to the partner's new technical contact so that they also have it on file

stem: An automation must generate a weekly compliance report every Monday at 07:00 from objects updated during the previous week, and notify the compliance lead. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: A trigger on every object update during the week that regenerates the report each time any object changes
A Monday 07:00 schedule querying last week's updates, generating one report and notifying the lead
A manual button that the compliance lead clicks on Monday morning whenever they remember to
A daily schedule that sends seven partial reports per week to the compliance lead

stem: An automation retries a failing external call up to 20 times with no delay between attempts. When the external system is down, the automation hammers it and floods logs. What should change?

choices.text: Fewer retries with backoff and jitter, then a pending fallback and an owner alert
Remove retries entirely so that the automation fails on the first error every time
Increase retries to 100 so that the call eventually succeeds when the system comes back
Run the automation every second to keep trying

stem: An automation updates customer tiers nightly. A developer needs to change the tier rules while the automation is live and some runs are in progress. What should they do?

choices.text: Edit the rules mid-run so that remaining customers get the new rules and earlier ones keep the old rules
Change the rules in a copy of the automation and let both run every night
Change between runs, test first, and record the rule version applied to each customer
Disable the automation permanently and update tiers manually from now on

stem: An automation's effect calls an Action, and the effect history shows failures with "submission criteria not met". The automation's condition matched. What is the likely explanation?

choices.text: Automations cannot call Actions, so the effect should be removed
The Action's submission criteria are always ignored for automations, so this error message must be impossible
The automation is broken and must be recreated from scratch
The condition matched but the Action's criteria rejected it at execution; align them

stem: Which situation is the clearest case for an event-triggered automation rather than a schedule?

choices.text: Recalculating customer lifetime value once per week
Archiving all closed tickets older than one year every night
Notifying an on-call engineer as soon as an incident's severity is raised to Critical
A monthly summary of all incidents sent to leadership on the first business day

stem: A team moves an automation from a personal project into a team project. They want failures to reach the team and the automation to keep running if its creator leaves. What should be configured?

choices.text: Keep the creator as owner and execution identity, and forward failure emails manually
Ask every team member to create their own copy of the automation
Give the automation administrator rights so that it never depends on anyone's permissions
Team ownership, a team execution identity, the right project scope and team-routed alerts

stem: An automation that creates invoices on order completion produced two invoices for some orders after a platform hiccup caused events to be redelivered. What design prevents this?

choices.text: Create invoices idempotently, checking for an existing one or using a deterministic key
Ask the platform team to guarantee exactly-once delivery for all events in the future
Disable the automation during platform maintenance windows
Delete duplicate invoices manually after each incident

stem: Before turning on a new automation that sends payment reminders to customers, the team wants to confirm it will contact the right customers with the right amounts. What should they do?

choices.text: Turn it on for all overdue customers at once and check a small sample of the emails that were sent the next morning
Test with representative objects and test recipients, then enable for a small monitored segment
Trust the conditions because they were written carefully
Enable it and ask customers to report errors
